# Count table
![](images/counts.png){style="width:200px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"}

The count table for MaAsLin3 needs to be a `data.frame` with:

- Columns names of features
    - In our case species
- Row names of sample names
- Values of counts
    - In our case abundance values

:::{.callout-note}
As it requires row names the count table cannot be a tibble.
:::

## Extract count table
![](images/extractor_fan_ibm_1.png){style="width: 200px; border-radius:5px;  background-color: white; border: 10px solid white" fig-align="center"}

Extract the `otu_table` (i.e. count table) from the genus `phyloseq` object as a `matrix`.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#Extract otu_table as matrix
taxa_df <- genus_pseq |>
    microbiome::abundances()
#Check
taxa_df[1:5,1:10]
```


## Formatting
![](images/format.png){style="width:100px; background:white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 7px" fig-align="center"}

Our count table is currently not in the correct format so we will need to use some base R and [`dplyr()`](https://cgr-liverpool.github.io/Tidyverse/dplyr/dplyr.html) functions to manipulate it. 
This includes:

- Transposing the table with `t()`
- Convert `matrix` to a `data.frame`
    - This is carried out after transposing as `t()` always produces a `matrix`
- Ensure all values are numerics
- Replacing `NA`s with 0 as MaAsLin3 won't work with `NA`s

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#Format count table for MaAsLin3
taxa_df <- taxa_df |>
    #Transpose and convert to data.frame
    t() |> as.data.frame() |>
    #Ensure all values are numerics
    dplyr::mutate_all(as.numeric)
#Replace an NAs with 0
taxa_df[is.na(taxa_df)] <- 0
#Check
taxa_df[1:5,1:10]
```

Perfect! Now its on to the metadata.
